STRL appears to be the most node-pure public candidate found in this pass because it explicitly combines data-center site development and mission-critical electrical services, with 2025 growth driven by higher data-center volume.

EME and FIX are direct construction-capacity candidates; both need margin-quality checks because data-center backlog can still fail the Serenity test if projects convert into low-margin or delayed work.

PWR is a second-order grid/interconnection candidate rather than a site builder; include in this node because power availability and utility construction often determine whether permitted data-center sites can be energized.

ACM is a permitting/environmental/planning hypothesis candidate; direct AI revenue sensitivity is less proven than for contractors, but its service menu aligns with local-regulatory, water, power and environmental bottlenecks.

Add STRL as a high-priority node candidate for AI data-center site development and mission-critical e-infrastructure; evidence strength is high because management discloses mission-critical backlog mix.

The node should be tracked as a physical-delivery chokepoint: entitled land, power access, water/discharge permits, local zoning, construction labor, MEP commissioning and project-risk transfer.
